@graph.name: White-Glove Delivery
@graph.description: White-glove delivery from The Flat Rate Movers — the top level of final-mile delivery and the handling standard for high-value, fragile and heavy pieces. White-glove delivery means the item crosses the threshold: brought in on a planned route, set in its final position, packaging removed and condition verified with the recipient before the crew leaves — never left at a curb. Each piece is assessed on its own — weight, fragile points, finish and value at risk — then wrapped, padded or crated to match: furniture and pieces travel fully covered in padded blankets and sealed with clear stretch wrap, and pieces that need more get a custom crate built around them. Antiques, art, pianos and instruments are the everyday work of this service. Behind the delivery sits the company's own final-mile chain — freight received and counted on the warehouse floor, staged, deconsolidated or cross-docked, and delivered in by the crew that handled it, with no hand-off to an unknown last carrier. A high-value delivery of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs — a safe, a piano, medical equipment — is surveyed and floor-checked to L/360 under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol before it is scheduled. Every job is quoted at one flat rate agreed in writing before dispatch; no rate schedule is published for this service. Assembly and installation are not published as scope, and haul-away of old items is not published as part of the service. Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free!

acceptedAnswer.text: White-glove delivery means the item crosses the threshold: brought in on a planned route, set in its final position, packaging removed and condition verified with you before the crew leaves — never left at a curb. It is the top level of final-mile delivery: room of choice plus unpacking, inspection with the recipient, and packaging and debris removal.

mainEntity.name: How are items protected for a white-glove delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each piece is assessed on its own — weight, fragile points, finish and value at risk — and the protection is matched to the piece: items travel fully covered in padded blankets and sealed with clear stretch wrap, or in a custom crate built around the piece when the piece demands it.

mainEntity.name: What kinds of items does white-glove delivery cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Antiques, art, pianos and instruments are the everyday work of this service, along with high-value and fragile freight generally. The heavy examples the pages name are a safe, a piano and medical equipment — pieces of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, which join the SIR plan before they move.

mainEntity.name: What happens with a heavy white-glove delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: A high-value delivery that weighs 1,500 to 3,500 lbs — a safe, a piano, medical equipment — is surveyed and floor-checked to L/360 under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol like any SIR move, so placement never becomes an improvisation at your door.

mainEntity.name: What are the delivery levels, and where does white glove sit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Curbside (left at the curb or driveway); threshold (carried inside the first door, garage or lobby); room of choice (carried to the room the recipient picks, no unpacking); room of choice with packaging removal; and white glove at the top (room of choice plus unpacking, inspection with the recipient, and packaging and debris removal). Some providers add assembly or installation above white glove. The ladder is industry vocabulary — no regulator defines these names.

mainEntity.name: What should you confirm before you book?

acceptedAnswer.text: Confirm in writing, whichever level you are buying: the endpoint (curb, first door, or a named room — and whether stairs are included); unpacking; packaging removal and what it excludes; assembly and installation; the appointment, who must be present, and whether a signature is required; inspection at signing, with condition recorded before the paperwork is signed; and the failed-delivery answer — what happens, and who pays, if the item cannot be carried in.

Sometimes in the industry — and only when it is agreed. Industry descriptions list assembly among the things white-glove service may include, and the scope depends on the carrier and the agreement, so it has to be confirmed before booking. On our side the answer is plain: assembly and installation are not part of our published scope. If a delivery turns on either, settle it with us when the job is scoped.

mainEntity.name: Is debris removal included with a delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often at the white-glove tier, but it should still be confirmed before booking — and confirm what the words cover. Removing the delivered item's own packaging is one service; hauling away the old item it replaces is another, and the second is not implied by the first. Our published practice covers the delivered item's packaging; haul-away of old items is not published as part of our service.

mainEntity.name: Can a white-glove delivery be scheduled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — appointment-based delivery is the norm for freight of any size. White-glove services commonly run on scheduled appointment windows, and retail freight deliveries are typically arranged on an appointment with a signature required. Our deliveries are arranged by appointment too; no fixed window length is published — the appointment is set when the job is scoped and quoted.

mainEntity.name: Is white-glove delivery available for residences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. White-glove service is frequently used for residential freight shipments — furniture, appliances, electronics, medical equipment and other big or high-value pieces. Our deliveries run to homes as well as to offices, industrial sites and retail spaces, dispatched from the Winchester and Martinsburg branches. A residence with stairs or a heavy piece is exactly the delivery to confirm in detail before the day.

mainEntity.name: Why does white-glove delivery cost more than curbside?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the service is different work, not a different label. White-glove pricing carries two-person teams, the scheduling coordination of an appointment, the extra time to carry, place, unpack and inspect, and the liability management of handling heavy or high-value freight inside the building. A curbside price stops at the curb — and hands you the carry, the placement and the stair risk.

mainEntity.name: What should I check before I sign for a delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check the item in its final position before the paperwork is signed: finish, corners, doors and drawers, and whether it is complete. Note any damage on the delivery documents, not after the crew has gone. Our crews verify condition with you before they leave.
